title: Duchy of Milan
capsule: The Duchy of Milan was created in 1395 when Holy Roman Emperor Wenceslaus granted Gian Galeazzo Visconti the ducal title, elevating what had been the Lordship of Milan into a hereditary duchy controlling much of Lombardy. Under the Sforza dynasty — established when Francesco I Sforza seized power in 1450 following the brief Ambrosian Republic — Milan became a leading Italian power and a centre of Renaissance patronage, hosting Leonardo da Vinci at the court of Ludovico il Moro. French invasion in 1499 inaugurated decades of contested Habsburg–Valois control; the death of the last Sforza duke, Francesco II, in 1535 without heirs prompted Charles V to govern Milan directly, and it passed by inheritance and treaty to Spanish then Austrian Habsburgs.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's core Lombard territory is well-documented in diplomatic records; boundaries fluctuated significantly during the Italian Wars (1494–1559) and are known from treaties and chronicles with moderate precision.
